The honest finding, stated up front, is that the market has largely identified this layer as well. What survives the work is one asymmetric name and a short watch list, and the discipline of saying so is the point of the piece. [...] One distinction has to come first. Two separate production flows feed an AI accelerator, and they are routinely conflated. The first is the HBM stack itself: thinning each DRAM die, forming the vertical interconnects, bonding the dies, and filling the gaps. The second is the package substrate that carries the logic die and the HBM stacks together. The stack flow is driven directly by HBM die volume. The substrate flow is driven by accelerator package count and complexity, where HBM is one input among several. Suppliers in the first flow have cleaner exposure to HBM unit growth. Suppliers in the second are exposed to AI accelerator demand more broadly. Keeping the two apart prevents the common error of treating every name here as a direct proxy for HBM. [...] The substrate node builds the FC-BGA package everything sits on, where the binding constraint is yield, not throughput.
